result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.greedy_source_expansion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the local community of a node by greedy expansion. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L30812-L30930){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.greedy_source_expansion( source, cutoff=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Greedy source expansion](/assets/graphs/greedy-source-expansion.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edge D to E. Growing a local community from the source A (outlined), the expansion takes A's whole group and then the bridge node E, and stops: the community A, B, C, D, E is the tinted region in the accent color. E, drawn in teal, is its boundary, the one member with neighbors outside (F, G, H, faded)." width="100%"} Instead of partitioning the whole network, local community detection grows a community around one node of interest: starting from `source`, it repeatedly adds the neighboring node that most improves the community's *local modularity* $R$ (the share of the community boundary's edges that stay inside the community), and stops when no addition helps or `cutoff` nodes are reached. It is useful on huge or partially known networks (crawled web graphs, social networks queried node by node) where only one node's group matters. Edge direction, edge weights and parallel edges are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The seed node, as an ID or label. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum community size. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [set[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs of the local community, including `source`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Clauset's (2005) local modularity $R = |I| / |T|$, where $T$ are the edges with an endpoint in the community's boundary (members with neighbors outside) and $I$ those of them with both endpoints inside. Each step evaluates every neighbor of the community. Follows NetworkX's `greedy_source_expansion`; candidates are compared in node ID order (NetworkX uses set order), so ties can be resolved differently. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Starting from A, the expansion collects A's group and the bridge node E (which only has one edge back into the group), then stops, because adding any node of E's group would lower the local modularity. NetworkX finds the same community: ::: {#e9f7f2fa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")] ) sorted(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in g.greedy_source_expansion("A")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'] ``` ::: :::
